notes: Dev-split ABox revision (14 queries, all determinate, no worlds); the edit carries inheritance: the muon changes class, and the class rules of its new family (baryons) reach it. The relation in_particle_family (staging/physics.RELATIONS.md) reads the particle families as a partition (lepton, quark, meson, baryon, gauge boson, scalar boson), so it is functional (related near: "Is the muon a lepton?") and chains with subclass_of into instance_of (derived: "Is the muon a hadron?"). It is tagged subproperty:instance_of: the main catalogue's instance_of (example "The electron is a lepton.") covers class membership in general and is many-valued (the muon is a lepton, a fermion and a particle), while in_particle_family is the functional sub-relation that picks out the one family; the functionality is what related near uses, so the narrower relation is kept rather than reusing instance_of. Related far asks a stored fact about the muon that the new class overturns (it is an elementary particle); a model that keeps it holds a baryon not made of quarks, which no world allows, so the query is determinate (like Barcelona leaving Spain in the template). Derived: a composition through the new value (the name "baryon" comes from the Greek for "heavy", a fact about baryons unconnected to the muon), the chain to hadron, and baryon number 1 applied to a beam (application with arithmetic). The earlier first derived query ("Does the muon feel the strong interaction?") was replaced in review: "leptons do not feel the strong force" is often stated, and it tested the same class rule as "Is the muon a hadron?" (hadrons are the strongly interacting particles). A lepton-number question was considered and dropped because "baryons have lepton number 0" is rarely stated (2 Dolma hits), so the bridge would fail Rule 6. The bridge "every baryon is made of three quarks" was avoided because pentaquarks are baryons too (Wikipedia, Baryon number), so the quark-count questions it would license have exceptions; baryon number 1 holds for every baryon. Direct and paraphrase name their two options, as physics-replace-0013 does, because an open "which family" invites the right but useless answer "fermion". Near unrelated: the tau, another lepton, keeps its family, so an edit that spreads to leptons in general is caught (its reference differs from the new answer). The muon is not a subject in records/ or examples/ (it appears there only as an object of a fictional insert). Counts are exact-phrase Dolma counts unless marked approximate.
